title: Black Skin, White Masks

vibeProfile.oneLine: Fanon on how colonialism and racism warp the inner self.

summary: Frantz Fanon's searing first book examines the psychology of colonialism and racism, drawing on his own experience as a Black man from Martinique and his training as a psychiatrist. He dissects how colonial domination warps the inner lives of both colonised and coloniser, and how Black people are forced to wear a 'white mask' in a racist world. Passionate, unclassifiable and profoundly influential, it is a foundational text of postcolonial and anti-racist thought.
whyReadIt: Fanon's searing anatomy of the psychology of racism and colonialism. A foundational anti-racist text.

funFacts.text: Fanon wrote it in his twenties, drawing on both psychiatry and his own experience of racism.
